The uniform distribution is very simple, but it occurs commonly in applications. The probability density function for this distribution on the interval 3a, b4 is
ƒ(x) = 1 b - a, a … x … b.

If each outcome in the sample space is equally likely to occur, then the random variable X has a uniform distribution. Since ƒ is constant on 3a, b4 , a random variable with a uni- form distribution is just as likely to be in one subinterval of a fixed length as in any other of the same length. The probability that X assumes a value in a subinterval of 3a, b4 is the length of that subinterval divided by (b - a).
